title: How to Buy a Used Gas Turbine Safely: NCNDA, LOI and Proof of Funds
html:
A used gas turbine costs several million dollars, and several intermediaries often market the same unit at once. That attracts serious sellers and also fraud. The process you insist on is your best protection. This guide explains the usual steps and the warning signs.

Why sellers hold back information

The owner, the exact location and the price of a unit are commercially sensitive. If a broker published them, other parties would bypass the chain within days. So each side reveals more as the other side shows it is real. Confidentiality at the start is normal.

The steps in order

  1. Letter of Intent (LOI). The buyer names the unit, the quantity and the intention to buy subject to inspection.
  2. Proof of funds. A bank-confirmed document shows that the buyer can pay. A screenshot of an account balance does not count.
  3. NCNDA. A non-circumvention and non-disclosure agreement protects all parties before serial numbers, location and owner are disclosed.
  4. Documents and inspection. The buyer receives the technical documentation and inspects the actual unit, in person or through an independent inspector.
  5. Payment. Payment runs through an independent escrow account or a documentary letter of credit.

Export control and sanctions rules apply to every deal. Destination and end user are screened before a contract is signed.

Warning signs of a fake listing

  • The seller asks for a deposit or a fee to a private or company account.
  • The seller demands an inspection fee before you have seen any document.
  • You have shown proof of funds, but the seller shows no title, mandate or serial numbers in return.
  • The seller creates pressure: another buyer pays today, the price is valid for 24 hours.
  • The same unit appears in many listings at different prices, and the photos do not match the specification.

Buying through LKS 360-SCHREINER LLC

LKS 360-SCHREINER LLC acts as independent broker for used and surplus gas turbines, steam turbines and gensets. The units belong to their owners. You find the current list in our catalogue Inventory.

This article is general guidance. It is no legal or export control advice.

title: Coal plant today, CO2-free iron power tomorrow: same turbine
html:
Coal plant today. CO2-free iron power tomorrow. Same turbine.

At TU Darmstadt, researchers burn iron powder instead of coal. The result is rust, not CO2. Green hydrogen turns the rust back into iron, and the iron burns again. The researchers call the loop near-lossless.

What this means for plant owners:
A 2026 KIT study finds that converting a coal plant mostly means adapting the heat generator. Steam cycle, turbine and generator stay in place.

The opportunity:
615 MW steam turbine generator set, new and never operated, rated up to 750 MW, complete with boiler, condenser and three warehouses of spare parts. Priced roughly 50 % below a comparable new build.

Run it on coal now. Convert it when iron power is ready. TU Darmstadt already operates a 1 MW pilot plant, and the researchers expect industrial scale from around 2030.

Once conversions start, steam turbine sets like this will be in demand. A new, never-operated 615 MW set at half the new-build price will not come back.

Price and full data with your LOI.
LKS 360-SCHREINER LLC | manager@lks360.com

Sources: TU Darmstadt (Clean Circles, Metal Energy Hub), KIT study 2026.

title: Iron fuel for 60 Hz grids: why existing steam sets matter
html:
Iron burns, gets heavier, and releases no CO2.

Fine iron powder burns to iron oxide and releases high-temperature heat. Green hydrogen reduces the oxide back to iron. The iron powder stores for months with little loss.

Why this matters for steam plant owners:

A 2026 KIT study (Schuler et al., Chem Circularity) finds that converting a coal plant to iron fuel centers on rebuilding the heat generator. Steam cycle, turbine and generator can in theory stay. TU Darmstadt opened its Metal Energy Hub in 2025 with a pilot line of about 1 MW.

Why 60 Hz markets should look now:

A steam turbine-generator set is built for one frequency. A 60 Hz set runs at 3,600 rpm and cannot operate in a 50 Hz grid. In the Americas, parts of Asia and the Middle East, existing 60 Hz steam sets can become the base of iron-ready capacity: dispatchable today, CO2-free tomorrow.

Planning baseload or seasonal storage on 60 Hz? Send me your MW, current fuel and timeline: manager@lks360.com or WhatsApp +49 170 4656619.

Sources: Schuler et al., A new iron age? Chem Circularity 2026 (KIT) · TU Darmstadt, Metal Energy Hub
